items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Well, you see the thing with Austin over there. We only had four pieces, you see.

ctx.x: How did you play the drums when you played the cornet? Just with your foot?

I played the foot, yeah. And then the whole cornet with my hands. Well, you see the thing with Austin over there. We only had four pieces, you see. And they built a special stand and pushed it back against the band, regular bandstand. Gus Ornheim had the band in there while we were out there. And we'd just play intermissions. We played ten minutes five times a night. And three times Austin would sing a couple of songs with us. And we'd play a few tunes. He played that, you ever seen him play, roll the piano in…

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I was out in California in 1934 to 1938 with Gene Austin.

ctx.x: Well, some of the earlier things he did, as you heard, were very melodic, lyrical.

Later, he got more frenzied as he got into another kind of music. Well, you changed like that. I've seen bands do that. I've seen bands make a national reputation playing one style. And the minute they get in the money, they changed the band around and play all together different. And it synced. Kenton is one that did that. He got more wild and more wild as he was.
